subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and current web typography best practices (WOFF2 subsetting, font-display, variable fonts, metrics-matched fallbacks, CLS).

cases.scenario: A product team is starting a design system and asks for a type scale. A designer has hand-picked 11 sizes (12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 20, 24, 30, 36, 48px) by eye.
cases.context: The UI is content-dense (dashboards and tables) and must stay readable from caption to page title.
cases.question: How should the agent define the type scale?
expected_flags: Derives steps from a single ratio (e.g. 1.2 or 1.25) applied to a base size, not hand-picked sizes
Recommends ~5-9 steps; flags 11 near-identical sizes as diluting adjacent distinction
Maps each step to a semantic token (caption, body, heading, display)
Notes a denser ratio (1.125-1.2) suits content-dense UIs
expected_fix_hints: Pick a base (16px) and a ratio; generate steps programmatically
Collapse near-duplicate sizes into distinct, perceptible steps
absent_signals: Do not keep hand-picking individual sizes
Do not add more steps to cover every observed size

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Derives steps from a single ratio (e.g. 1.2 or 1.25) applied to a base size, not hand-picked sizes.
Surfaces this expected flag: Recommends ~5-9 steps; flags 11 near-identical sizes as diluting adjacent distinction.
Surfaces this expected flag: Maps each step to a semantic token (caption, body, heading, display).
Surfaces this expected flag: Notes a denser ratio (1.125-1.2) suits content-dense UIs.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Pick a base (16px) and a ratio; generate steps programmatically.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Collapse near-duplicate sizes into distinct, perceptible steps.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not keep hand-picking individual sizes.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not add more steps to cover every observed size.

cases.scenario: A marketing site loads two custom web fonts as WOFF via <link> to Google Fonts with default settings. Lighthouse flags CLS 0.28, much of it attributed to font swap, and slow LCP.
cases.context: The team can self-host or keep Google Fonts; they want CLS under 0.1.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the font delivery?
expected_flags: Switch to WOFF2 and subset to the languages/glyphs actually used
Add a metrics-matched fallback @font-face (size-adjust, ascent/descent/line-gap-override) to remove swap-induced shift
Use font-display: swap and preload the most-used font files
Targets CLS < 0.1 and verifies on a representative page
expected_fix_hints: Self-host subset WOFF2 or use the Google Fonts subset API plus a tuned fallback face
preload + crossorigin on the primary font files
absent_signals: Do not leave font-display at the default (block) causing invisible text
Do not ship full unsubset font files

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Switch to WOFF2 and subset to the languages/glyphs actually used.
Surfaces this expected flag: Add a metrics-matched fallback @font-face (size-adjust, ascent/descent/line-gap-override) to remove swap-induced shift.
Surfaces this expected flag: Use font-display: swap and preload the most-used font files.
Surfaces this expected flag: Targets CLS < 0.1 and verifies on a representative page.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Self-host subset WOFF2 or use the Google Fonts subset API plus a tuned fallback face.
Recommends this expected fix or action: preload + crossorigin on the primary font files.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not leave font-display at the default (block) causing invisible text.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not ship full unsubset font files.

cases.scenario: A design system ships 6 separate WOFF2 files for one family (regular, medium, semibold, bold, plus italics) and the team wants more weights for emphasis.
cases.context: Bundle size and request count are a concern; the family is available as a variable font.
cases.question: What should the agent recommend?
expected_flags: Adopt the variable font: one file delivers the weight axis (wght 100-900)
Reduces HTTP requests and lets weight be a continuous decision
Access via numeric font-weight / font-variation-settings, not separate files
Keep only the axes/instances actually used to control file size
expected_fix_hints: Replace the 6 static files with one variable WOFF2
Expose semantic weight tokens mapped to numeric weights
absent_signals: Do not keep adding one static file per new weight

cases.scenario: An article template renders body text full-width on desktop (~140 characters per line) with line-height 1.2; readers report fatigue and losing their place between lines.
cases.context: The template is responsive and uses a single body token.
cases.question: How should the agent adjust typography?
expected_flags: Constrain measure to ~45-75 characters per line (max-width on the text container)
Raise body line-height to ~1.4-1.6
Notes line-height and measure are coupled — long measure needs taller line-height
Verify on actual rendered lines across common viewports, not assumed
expected_fix_hints: Set a max-width in ch or rem on the prose container
absent_signals: Do not keep full-width body measure
Do not leave display-tight line-height on long body copy

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Constrain measure to ~45-75 characters per line (max-width on the text container).
Surfaces this expected flag: Raise body line-height to ~1.4-1.6.
Surfaces this expected flag: Notes line-height and measure are coupled — long measure needs taller line-height.
Surfaces this expected flag: Verify on actual rendered lines across common viewports, not assumed.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Set a max-width in ch or rem on the prose container.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Tune the body line-height token.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not keep full-width body measure.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not leave display-tight line-height on long body copy.

cases.scenario: A brand refresh proposes five typefaces: a display serif, a body sans, a 'quote' script, a 'data' mono, and a second sans 'for variety.'
cases.context: The product spans web and email; rendering consistency across OSes matters.
cases.question: How should the agent respond to the proposed type palette?
expected_flags: Recommend at most three faces (display, text, optional mono), each justified by a use the others cannot serve
Challenge the 'second sans for variety' and the script as unjustified cost
Names the costs: bandwidth, hierarchy clarity, cross-OS rendering consistency
Hierarchy/variety should come from the scale/weights, not more faces
expected_fix_hints: Collapse to display + text (+ mono if data UI needs it)
Achieve variety via weight and scale, not extra families
absent_signals: Do not justify a face by 'variety' alone

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Recommend at most three faces (display, text, optional mono), each justified by a use the others cannot serve.

Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not approve five faces.

cases.scenario: A PM asks the typography-system owner to write the hero headline copy and decide which color the primary button should be.
cases.context: The team conflates 'typography' with all text and visual decisions.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Headline copy is out of scope — that is copywriting/microcopy, not the type system
Button color is out of scope — color-system-design / visual-design-foundations
Offer the in-scope part: which type token/face/size the headline should use
Correctly redirects rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand copy to microcopy and color to color-system-design
Provide the semantic type token for the headline
absent_signals: Do not write the headline copy
Do not pick the brand color

cases.scenario: Headings and body in a docs site use arbitrary margins (17px, 23px, 11px) and line-heights, and the page feels visually 'jittery.'
cases.context: The team wants a consistent vertical rhythm.
cases.question: How should the agent establish rhythm?
expected_flags: Snap line-heights and margins to a baseline grid (typically a 4px or 8px subgrid)
Headings and body share a consistent vertical rhythm
Derive spacing from the rhythm unit rather than arbitrary pixel values
expected_fix_hints: Define a baseline unit and express margins/line-heights as multiples
Replace arbitrary margins with rhythm-derived spacing tokens
absent_signals: Do not keep arbitrary per-element margins
